principles.primary_measurement: count eligible user events as close to the application boundary as practical

low_traffic_strategy: aggregate only operations with the same consequence
use an explicitly reviewed time-based or user-minute method when event ratios are too sparse

objectives.description: eligible order attempts receive a reconciled successful outcome
objectives.eligible_event: authorized, syntactically valid order attempts admitted at the application boundary
objectives.good_event: the API returns the declared success result and the idempotency token resolves to exactly one committed order

objectives.description: eligible order attempts complete within the user latency threshold
objectives.eligible_event: the same admitted attempts used by SLO-AVAILABILITY
objectives.good_event: the final reconciled response completes within 250 ms

objectives.description: a routed read observes the selected committed order within the declared freshness bound
objectives.eligible_event: synthetic or production-authorized probes carrying a known commit token
objectives.good_event: the chosen read path returns the committed token within 5 seconds
objectives.measurement_point: read entrypoint using a commit-correlated probe
objectives.forbidden_shortcut: wall-clock age of pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp without a current write or commit token

objectives.description: no acknowledged order may violate uniqueness, tenant, amount, or state-transition invariants
objectives.success_condition: scheduled and incident reconciliation finds zero unexplained mismatches
objectives.failure_action: page and freeze affected writes; do not spend a ratio error budget to excuse corruption

objectives.description: a restore procedure remains executable and produces checked application state
objectives.success_condition: an isolated restore drill passes at least every 90 days and after material recovery-path changes
objectives.failure_action: block high-risk release and open an owned remediation

default_exclusions.condition: request is rejected before admission because it violates the published syntax contract
authentication or authorization correctly rejects an identity outside the service contract
default_exclusions.justification: a correct security denial is not availability failure

default_exclusions.condition: the client disconnects before the service accepts work and no server-side outcome exists
default_exclusions.justification: the service did not admit the event

actions: require service and platform owner exception for material changes
open an incident or reliability review
resume only through a recorded joint decision

gaming_prohibited: reclassifying failures as maintenance after the event
moving the measurement point farther from users to hide errors
combining unrelated high-volume operations to drown a low-volume critical path
